newsitem.title: USA: US rep offers ANWR coastal plain wilderness bill.
newsitem.headline: US rep offers ANWR coastal plain wilderness bill.

text.p: Minnesota Democratic Representative Bruce Vento introduced a bill to designate the 1.5 million acre coastal plain of the Arctic National Wildlife Refuge as protected wilderness, which would bar oil and natural gas development. Vento in a statement said wilderness designation, which would prohibit commercial operations, motorized access, roads and other facilities, "...is needed to prevent the destruction of this irreplaceable resource." Alaska's congressional delegation has pushed opening ANWR's coastal plain to oil development, saying it could be done without significant harm to the environment and would be an economic boost for their state. But environmental groups -- and the Clinton administration -- say development would destroy the fragile arctic ecosystem that supports a vast array of wildlife. Clinton vetoed a budget bill last year partly because it had language to allow ANWR development.
